script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

TITLE: GROCERY STORY

INT. SUPERMARKET - DAY

A bustling SUPERMARKET, filled with shoppers, EMPLOYEES scurrying about, and the ever-present background hum of customers' chatter and cash registers ringing.

Enter JESS, a young, dedicated ASSISTANT MANAGER, mid-twenties, with her arms overflowing with grocery bags. She looks harried and flustered.

ASSISTANT MANAGER (JESS)
(To herself)
Two hours. I have two hours to get all this stuff put away.

INT. SUPERMARKET - EMPLOYEE BREAK ROOM - LATER

Jess enters the dimly lit EMPLOYEE BREAK ROOM, drops her bags on a table, and slumps down into a chair, defeated.

ASSISTANT MANAGER (JESS)
(Muttering)
I hate Mondays.

A door creaks open, and in walks ANNA, an older, more experienced EMPLOYEE, in her late thirties. She carries a single reusable grocery bag and gives Jess a sympathetic smile.

EMPLOYEE (ANNA)
You'll get through it, Jess. It's only a few hours.

Jess lets out a small laugh, shaking her head.

ASSISTANT MANAGER (JESS)
Yeah, you'd think so, but sometimes it feels like the entire world depends on me getting every single item in the right place at the right time.

EMPLOYEE (ANNA)
Well, it does. But you've got this. And I'm here to help.

INT. SUPERMARKET - AISLE 7 - LATER

Jess and Anna work together, restocking shelves. They laugh and share stories about their past experiences.

ASSISTANT MANAGER (JESS)
Remember that time we had to deal with the great yogurt spill of '18?

EMPLOYEE (ANNA)
Oh, how could I forget? We were covered in strawberry, vanilla, and chocolate for hours!

They both laugh, and their camaraderie is palpable.

INT. SUPERMARKET - CUSTOMER SERVICE - LATER

Jess is helping a customer, LUCY, an elderly woman, when Anna appears, offering to take over.

ASSISTANT MANAGER (JESS)
Thanks, Anna. I've got this.

EMPLOYEE (ANNA)
You sure? I'd be happy to help.

ASSISTANT MANAGER (JESS)
No, I've got it. It's just a small favor. Besides, I appreciate the offer.

Lucy smiles warmly at Jess and pats her hand.

CUSTOMER (LUCY)
You're a good girl, dear. Keep up the good work.

INT. SUPERMARKET - EMPLOYEE BREAK ROOM - NIGHT

Jess and Anna sit together in the break room, enjoying a well-deserved snack.

ASSISTANT MANAGER (JESS)
You know, I don't think I could have made it through today without you.

EMPLOYEE (ANNA)
And I wouldn't have wanted to make it through without you, Jess. We make a great team.

They share a smile, their friendship growing stronger with each passing day.

INT. SUPERMARKET - NEXT DAY

Jess arrives at work, ready to face another day, but this time she does so with a renewed sense of confidence. She knows that, no matter what challenges come her way, she has Anna by her side.

ASSISTANT MANAGER (JESS)
(To herself)
Bring it on. We've got this.

Fade to black.

THE END
